headline: This 2022 law updates federal rules so GSA-managed public buildings use the most cost-effective, energy-efficient lighting systems available.
what_it_does: The law expands existing requirements for energy-efficient lighting in federal buildings that the General Services Administration builds or manages. Buildings must now use the most life-cycle cost-effective and energy-efficient lighting systems available, including items such as sensors and fixture layout. It also sets rules for how the government buys these lighting systems. Finally, it requires GSA to share information on buying and using these systems with federal, state, local, and tribal governments.

who_it_affects.how: They must equip and buy lighting for GSA-managed public buildings under the updated efficiency and procurement rules.
They can receive GSA information about buying and using energy-efficient lighting systems.

who_it_affects.group: companies that sell lighting products to the federal government
who_it_affects.how: Federal purchasing of lighting systems is now governed by more specific procurement requirements.
